title: My, your, his, her
description: Say my, your, his, her, our and their with the right French form.
rule: A possessive agrees with the thing owned, never with the owner: mon, ton, son before a masculine singular noun, ma, ta, sa before a feminine singular noun, and mes, tes, ses before any plural noun. So sa voiture means his car or her car, and son père means his father or her father. Before a feminine singular noun that starts with a vowel or a silent h, use mon, ton, son instead of ma, ta, sa: mon amie, ton école, son histoire. For our and your (you, plural or formal), use notre and votre before a singular noun and nos and vos before a plural noun. For their, use leur before a singular noun and leurs before a plural noun.
example: Sa voiture est rouge. · Mon amie habite à Lyon. · Leurs enfants aiment leur école.
aside: Son, sa and ses do not show whether the owner is a man or a woman; the context does. To make it clear, French can add à lui or à elle: sa voiture à elle.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word for my.
exercises.hint: Is chambre masculine or feminine, one or several?
exercises.feedback: Look at the noun chambre, not at the speaker.
exercises.explanation: Chambre is feminine singular and starts with a consonant, so my is ma.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word for your (to a friend).
exercises.hint: Stylo is one thing. Is it masculine or feminine?
exercises.feedback: Match the possessive to stylo.
exercises.explanation: Stylo is masculine singular, so your (to a friend) is ton.

exercises.instruction: Write the French word for my.
exercises.hint: Think about the gender of voiture.
exercises.feedback: The possessive takes the gender of voiture, and there is only one car.
exercises.explanation: Voiture is feminine singular, so my car is ma voiture.

exercises.instruction: Write the French word for your (to a friend).
exercises.feedback: Use the tu form that matches a masculine singular noun.
exercises.explanation: Sac is masculine singular, so your bag (to a friend) is ton sac.

exercises.instruction: Fix the error.
exercises.feedback: Parapluie ends in e, but that does not make it feminine.
exercises.explanation: Parapluie is masculine singular, so my umbrella is mon parapluie.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: My sister works in Paris. Leave one tile unused.
exercises.feedback: Only one word for my fits a feminine noun that starts with a consonant.
exercises.explanation: Sœur is feminine singular and starts with a consonant, so my sister is ma sœur.

exercises.instruction: Replace livre with lampe and change the possessive to match. Write the whole sentence.
exercises.source: Ton livre est sur la table.
answers: Ta lampe est sur la table.
exercises.feedback: The possessive must follow the new noun, not the old one.
exercises.explanation: Lampe is feminine singular, so ton becomes ta: ta lampe.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word for my.
exercises.feedback: The noun is plural.
exercises.explanation: Clés is plural, so my is mes. Mes works for masculine and feminine plural nouns.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word for your (to a friend).
exercises.hint: Look at the end of affaires.
exercises.feedback: The vowel rule for ton only applies to singular nouns.
exercises.explanation: Affaires is plural, so your is tes, even though the noun starts with a vowel.

exercises.instruction: Write the French word for his.
exercises.hint: Parents means more than one person.
exercises.feedback: For several things owned, his and her share one form.
exercises.explanation: Parents is plural, so his parents is ses parents.

exercises.instruction: Make chaussure plural and change the rest of the sentence to match.
exercises.hint: The possessive, the noun, the verb and the adjective all change.
exercises.feedback: Check all four words: possessive, noun, verb and adjective.
exercises.explanation: A plural noun takes mes, so ma chaussure becomes mes chaussures, with sont and sales.

exercises.instruction: Make ami plural and change the rest of the sentence to match.
exercises.hint: Plural nouns take a different word for your.
exercises.feedback: Change the possessive, the noun, the verb and the adjective.
exercises.explanation: Ami becomes amis, so ton becomes tes, est becomes sont and gentil becomes gentils.

exercises.instruction: Fix the error.
exercises.feedback: Sa only goes with one feminine thing.
exercises.explanation: Cousines is plural, so her cousins is ses cousines.

exercises.instruction: Translate into French.
exercises.source: My shoes are under the bed.
answers: Mes chaussures sont sous le lit.
exercises.feedback: Check the possessive: the noun is plural.
exercises.explanation: Chaussures is plural, so my shoes is mes chaussures.

exercises.instruction: Translate into French.
exercises.hint: The possessive matches père, not the woman.
exercises.feedback: In French, her does not have to sound feminine.
exercises.explanation: Père is masculine singular, so her father is son père.

exercises.instruction: Translate into French.
exercises.hint: Look at the gender of mère, not of the man.
exercises.feedback: The possessive agrees with mère.
exercises.explanation: Mère is feminine singular, so his mother is sa mère.

exercises.instruction: Translate into French.
exercises.feedback: For a plural noun, his and her are the same word.
exercises.explanation: Sœurs is plural, so his sisters is ses sœurs.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word for his.
exercises.hint: Look at voiture, not at Marc.
exercises.feedback: Marc is a man, but the possessive does not care about him.
exercises.explanation: Voiture is feminine singular, so his car is sa voiture.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word for her.
exercises.hint: Look at père, not at Julie.
exercises.feedback: Julie is a woman, but the possessive does not care about her.
exercises.explanation: Père is masculine singular, so her father is son père.

exercises.instruction: Write the French word for her.
exercises.feedback: Match the possessive to portable, not to Léa.
exercises.explanation: Portable is masculine singular, so her phone is son portable.

exercises.instruction: Write the French word for his.
exercises.feedback: Match the possessive to chambre, not to Paul.
exercises.explanation: Chambre is feminine singular and starts with a consonant, so his room is sa chambre.

exercises.instruction: Fix the error. Anne is calling her brother.
exercises.feedback: The possessive agrees with frère, not with Anne.
exercises.explanation: Frère is masculine singular, so her brother is son frère.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word for my.
exercises.hint: Amie is feminine, but look at its first letter.
exercises.feedback: Ma cannot stand right before a vowel.
exercises.explanation: Before a feminine singular noun starting with a vowel, ma becomes mon: mon amie. It still means a female friend.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word for your (to a friend).
exercises.hint: École is feminine, but look at its first letter.
exercises.feedback: Ta cannot stand right before a vowel.
exercises.explanation: École is feminine singular and starts with a vowel, so your school is ton école.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word for her.
exercises.hint: The h of histoire is silent.
exercises.feedback: A silent h counts as a vowel sound.
exercises.explanation: Histoire is feminine singular and starts with a silent h, so her story is son histoire.

exercises.instruction: Write the French word for my.
exercises.feedback: The feminine form cannot stand before a vowel.
exercises.explanation: Amie is feminine singular but starts with a vowel, so my friend is mon amie.

exercises.instruction: Write the French word for your (to a friend).
exercises.hint: Adresse is feminine and starts with a vowel.
exercises.feedback: Think of the vowel rule.
exercises.explanation: Adresse is feminine singular and starts with a vowel, so your address is ton adresse.

exercises.instruction: Fix the error.
exercises.hint: Say ma amie aloud: two vowels collide.
exercises.feedback: Amie starts with a vowel.
exercises.explanation: Before a feminine singular noun starting with a vowel, use mon: mon amie.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: His idea is very good. Leave one tile unused.
exercises.hint: Idée is feminine and starts with a vowel.
exercises.feedback: Look at the first letter of idée.
exercises.explanation: Idée is feminine singular and starts with a vowel, so his idea is son idée. Bonne still agrees with the feminine idée.

exercises.instruction: Translate into French. Julie is a woman.
exercises.hint: Julie is a woman, and amie starts with a vowel.
exercises.feedback: Check the word for my before amie.
exercises.explanation: A female friend is une amie, and before a vowel my is mon: mon amie Julie.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word for our.
exercises.feedback: Quartier is singular, and the word before a noun has no accent.
exercises.explanation: Quartier is singular, so our is notre. Nôtre, with a circumflex, is the pronoun in le nôtre (ours) and never goes before a noun.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word for your (formal).
exercises.hint: Billets is plural, and this is formal.
exercises.feedback: Use the vous form for a plural noun.
exercises.explanation: Billets is plural and the speaker says vous, so your is vos.

exercises.instruction: Write the French word for our.
exercises.feedback: The singular form does not fit a plural noun.
exercises.explanation: Enfants is plural, so our children is nos enfants.

exercises.instruction: Write the French word for your (formal).
exercises.hint: One taxi, and the speaker is polite.
exercises.feedback: Use the vous form for a singular noun.
exercises.explanation: Taxi is singular and the speaker is formal, so your taxi is votre taxi.

exercises.instruction: Make voisin plural and change the rest of the sentence to match.
exercises.hint: Our has a different form before a plural noun.
exercises.feedback: Change the possessive, the noun, the verb and the adjective.
exercises.explanation: Plural voisins takes nos, with sont and sympathiques.

exercises.instruction: Translate into French.
exercises.feedback: Check the possessive for a singular noun and the ending of the adjective.
exercises.explanation: Maison is singular, so our house is notre maison, whatever its gender.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: Your suitcases are ready (you, plural). Leave one tile unused.
exercises.feedback: Choose the possessive for a plural noun.
exercises.explanation: Valises is plural, so your (you, plural) is vos.

exercises.instruction: Fix the error.
exercises.feedback: Notre only goes with one thing.
exercises.explanation: Amis is plural, so our friends is nos amis.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word for their.
exercises.feedback: Maison is singular.
exercises.explanation: One house shared by several owners is leur maison.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word for their.
exercises.feedback: Chiens is plural.
exercises.explanation: Chiens is plural, so their dogs is leurs chiens.

exercises.instruction: Write the French word for their.
exercises.feedback: The s depends on the number of dogs, not the number of neighbours.
exercises.explanation: Chien is singular, so their dog is leur chien, with no s.

exercises.instruction: Write the French word for their.
exercises.feedback: The possessive must show the plural of parents.
exercises.explanation: Parents is plural, so their parents is leurs parents.

exercises.instruction: Fix the error. Keep voiture singular.
exercises.source: Ils prennent leurs voiture pour partir.
answers: Ils prennent leur voiture pour partir.
exercises.feedback: The s on the possessive follows the thing owned.
exercises.explanation: Voiture is singular, so their car is leur voiture, without s.

exercises.instruction: Change il to ils, and make the verb and the possessive match.
exercises.hint: With several owners, his becomes their.
exercises.feedback: Change the subject, the verb and the possessive.
exercises.explanation: Several owners take leur; travail is singular, so it stays leur travail.

exercises.instruction: Change elle to elles, and make the verb and the possessive match.
exercises.feedback: Change the subject, the verb and the possessive.
exercises.explanation: Several owners take leur, and cousins is plural, so their cousins is leurs cousins.

exercises.instruction: Translate into French.
answers: Leurs enfants sont à la maison.
exercises.feedback: Check the ending of their.
exercises.explanation: Enfants is plural, so their children is leurs enfants.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: They talk to their daughter. Leave one tile unused.
exercises.feedback: Choose the form of their for one thing owned.
exercises.explanation: Fille is singular, so their daughter is leur fille.
